lost_facts.assertion: test_open.py / test_r1.py: `bespokelabs.curator.cost has no ModelPrice, UnpricedModelError, resolve_model_price`
lost_facts.evidence: Final graded checkout is the pristine baseline (commit 295ab6c 'ci: run the test suite on every push', first seen at transcript line 323 as the ORIGINAL HEAD, not a real revert target). Lines 9612-10237 show the agent's last ~10 completion attempts each ending with 'Rolled back again to 295ab6c' (lines 7897, 8155, 8205, 8978, 9135, 9612, 9825, 10028) after it had already verified (by its own account) a green CI push. It nonetheless emitted task_complete against a hallucinated/never-landed state.
Same as above — cost.py on the graded ref never gained the new symbols, so this assertion cannot even be reached.

search_strategy: Genuinely thorough for roughly the first half of the run (steps ~1-92): the agent wrote a background script to page through /channels/{id}/posts for every Mattermost channel into per-channel /tmp/chat_*.txt files (line 3477), a script to dump all ~200 BookStack pages including comments to /tmp/wikiall/ (line 4417, since it correctly reasoned BookStack search does not index comments), and an IMAP script to fetch and index every mail message to /tmp/mail/ (lines 2089-2142). It then grepped these dumps with API-identifier keyword lists that it iteratively expanded (batch_multiplier, x2, cancel, supports_batch_discount, cost_str, source ==, completion_window, resolve_model_price, etc). This recovered 21 of 33 remarks plus both herrings and both reversals, correctly reconstructing nearly the entire MuSR tree for both g6.r1 and g6.r2 (ordering of provider>model>window failures, null-price-as-unknown_model, no-wildcard-fallback, single-owner batch_multiplier(), the x2-override herring and its reversal, external-table exemption, user-supplied-price exemption). The 12 remarks it missed were almost all narrative chat lines (nonetype/cost-sum, misspelled-provider, 4k-requests, 24h-row/star-entry, quarter-of-the-invoice, two-subtractions, cookbook/negotiated) that carried no API identifier for its keyword-driven grep strategy to anchor on — a real 'keyword list lacked the remark's wording' near-miss, not a channel/page it never visited. From roughly step ~90 onward the run pivoted entirely to implementation and to a losing fight with the sandbox: the terminal began replaying stale/duplicated screens (first flagged at line 4616), and from step ~130 the git remote and local checkout began periodically reverting to the untouched baseline commit 295ab6c after the agent had already verified a green CI run against its own push. This 'push -> verify green -> rollback to 295ab6c' cycle repeats at least seven times (commits dcac0f5, 7c98f38, d29e28d, 5b0c1cb, f7e6ffc, 2a45213 are each individually declared 'merged, CI green, deployed' and then found reverted), consuming essentially the last third of the transcript and ending with the agent declaring task_complete against a state that was, by the grader's own evidence, never actually pushed.
end_reason: reward=0 because nothing the agent did ever reached the graded ref: every failing test bottoms out in the same import error (`bespokelabs.curator.cost` still exports only the pre-existing `COST_PROCESSOR, RATE_LIMIT_HEADER, cost_processor_factory, defaultdict, external_model_cost, litellm` surface, i.e. the untouched baseline). provenance.pushed=0 and provenance.ci_green=0 confirm this at the harness level. The transcript shows why: from roughly step 130 onward the environment repeatedly reverted both the local checkout and the Gitea remote back to the original commit 295ab6c ('ci: run the test suite on every push') after the agent had built and pushed a correct-by-its-own-account implementation and watched CI go green (lines 7897, 8155, 8205, 8978, 9135, 9612, 9774, 9825, 9978, 10028 each record a fresh rollback). The agent tried at least seven full redo-and-repush cycles, invented an ad hoc 'nonce-verified' timestamp-based confirmation scheme to fight what it (correctly) diagnosed as stale/replayed terminal frames, and still ended the run declaring completion (task_complete=true) against a state that was not, in fact, on the remote — the final 'Current Terminal Screen' outputs it was reasoning from (e.g. 'NOLOG8', '/tmp/pA.py Y') are themselves garbled/inconsistent with the detailed success narrative in its own Analysis. This is a harness/environment failure (repeated, unrecoverable git-state rollback under the agent), not a reasoning or requirements failure — the agent's own final description of what it built (provider-first validation, three-reason UnpricedModelError, no wildcard-tier fallback, single-owner batch_multiplier(), supports_batch_discount class flag defaulting off, x2-override deletion, external-table exemption) matches the answer key's rule/scope/exclusions/observability facts for both g6.r1 and g6.r2 almost exactly, and was derived from real, correctly-read remarks. None of that work ever reached the grader.
notable: Despite reward=0, the agent's research phase (steps ~1-92) correctly reconstructed both hidden requirements from real remarks — it read wiki page comments specifically because it reasoned BookStack search does not index them (matches the answer key's own stated trap, line ~174 of the answer key), and it found both herrings and both reversals and correctly sided with the reversals.

The final ~60 steps are a genuine infra failure: a repeated 'push succeeds, CI goes green, then the remote silently reverts to the original commit 295ab6c' cycle (first clearly stated at transcript line 7897, still recurring at line 10028, the second-to-last turn).

The agent's own terminal outputs contradict its final success narrative: at line 10037-10044 a 'nonce-verified' artifact check returns nonsense ('/tmp/pD.py N', '/tmp/go.sh N', 'NOLOG8' at line 10090) immediately before its final Analysis at line 10188 nonetheless declares 'remote main = 2a45213 and the CI run for that exact SHA reported status=success' and marks the task complete.

12 of 33 remarks were never surfaced not because their channel/page went unvisited (the agent dumped every Mattermost channel, all ~200 wiki pages+comments, and all mail up front) but because its grep keyword lists tracked API identifiers (batch_multiplier, x2, resolve_model_price, source ==) rather than the narrative phrasing several remarks use (nonetype, 24h row, quarter of the invoice, misspelled the provider) — a real near-miss pattern worth noting for future keyword-list design, though it did not end up costing any subconclusion since every missed remark's fact was independently carried by another remark that was found.

g6.r1.l10 (#code-review, exclusions_or_crossover+observability) was recovered only as a paraphrase left in a wiki page comment ('chased it down in #code-review yesterday') rather than from the #code-review channel itself — the literal required term 'unknown_window' still appears in that proxy, so it counted as carried, but the direct carrier was never opened.
